learningObjectives.title: The unification of Italy and Germany
The Eastern Question and the Balkans
Colonial rivalries and the causes of WWI

questions.q: Who served as Prime Minister of Piedmont-Sardinia and used skilful diplomacy to advance Italian unification?
questions.explain: Cavour, PM of Piedmont-Sardinia, led the diplomatic drive that made his state the core of a united Italy.

questions.q: In which year was the Kingdom of Italy proclaimed with Victor Emmanuel II as its first king?
questions.explain: The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in 1861 under Victor Emmanuel II, though Venetia and Rome were added later.

questions.q: Why was Garibaldi's Expedition of the Thousand (1860) important for Italian unification?
options: It captured Sicily and Naples, bringing southern Italy into the new kingdom
It defeated Austria at the Battle of Sadowa
It secured Venetia directly from France
It captured Rome from the Pope
questions.explain: Garibaldi's Redshirts conquered the south, which he then handed to Victor Emmanuel II, uniting north and south.

questions.q: Which office did Otto von Bismarck hold from 1862 as he drove German unification?
questions.explain: Bismarck was appointed Minister-President of Prussia in 1862 and directed policy through the wars of unification.

questions.q: The German Empire was proclaimed in January 1871 in the Hall of Mirrors at which palace?
questions.explain: After defeating France, the German Empire was declared in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, with Wilhelm I as Kaiser.

questions.q: What did Bismarck mean by his 'blood and iron' speech of 1862?
options: That German unity would be achieved by military strength, not liberal speeches and votes
That Germany needed to expand its heavy industry to survive
That Prussia should adopt a liberal written constitution
That Austria should be allowed to lead unification
questions.explain: Bismarck argued that the great questions of the day would be settled by force ('iron and blood') rather than parliamentary debate.

questions.q: Why did Bismarck edit and publish the Ems telegram in 1870?
options: To provoke France into declaring war and unite the German states against a common enemy
To apologise to France for Prussian insults
To form a secret alliance with Austria
To warn Russia against interfering in Germany
questions.explain: Bismarck sharpened the telegram's wording to insult France, provoking a French declaration of war that rallied the German states behind Prussia.

questions.q: A source describes a secret 1858 meeting where Napoleon III promised Cavour French military help against Austria. This agreement was known as the:
questions.explain: At Plombieres in 1858, Napoleon III agreed to help Piedmont against Austria, leading to the war of 1859.

questions.q: The declining Ottoman Empire in the 19th century was commonly nicknamed the:
questions.explain: The Ottoman Empire's weakness led European powers to call it the 'sick man of Europe', fuelling the Eastern Question.

questions.q: Why was the Congress of Berlin held in 1878?
options: To revise the Treaty of San Stefano, as the powers feared a large Bulgaria under Russian influence
To divide Africa among the European powers
To bring an end to the Crimean War
questions.explain: Britain and Austria disliked the enlarged, Russian-influenced Bulgaria of San Stefano, so the Congress of Berlin reduced it.

questions.q: What was the main consequence of Austria-Hungary's annexation of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1908?
options: It angered Serbia and Russia, sharply heightening tension in the Balkans
It completed the unification of Italy
It brought about the immediate collapse of the Ottoman Empire
questions.explain: The 1908 annexation infuriated Serbia, which wanted the province, and its ally Russia, deepening Balkan rivalry.

questions.q: Why did Russia take a close interest in the Balkans and the Eastern Question?
options: It sought to protect fellow Slavs and gain access to warm-water routes through the straits
It wanted to acquire colonies in Africa
It aimed to lead the unification of Germany
It sought to annex the Italian peninsula
questions.explain: Pan-Slavism and the desire for access to the Mediterranean via the Black Sea straits drew Russia into Balkan affairs.

questions.q: Why did the Balkan Wars of 1912-13 increase the risk of a wider European war?
options: They greatly enlarged Serbia, alarming Austria-Hungary
They gave Germany new colonies in Morocco
questions.explain: A stronger, larger Serbia after the Balkan Wars alarmed Austria-Hungary, which feared Slav nationalism within its empire.

questions.q: After the Second Balkan War (1913) Serbia had roughly doubled in size. Which Great Power felt most threatened by a stronger Serbia?
questions.explain: A larger Serbia encouraged Slav nationalism inside Austria-Hungary, making the empire feel most threatened.

questions.q: Which three powers formed the Triple Alliance of 1882?
questions.explain: The Triple Alliance of 1882 bound Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy together in mutual defence.

questions.q: The Triple Entente was an understanding between which three powers?
questions.explain: The Triple Entente linked Britain, France and Russia, balancing the Triple Alliance before 1914.

questions.q: Who assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo on 28 June 1914?
questions.explain: Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb linked to the Black Hand, shot Franz Ferdinand, sparking the July Crisis.

questions.q: Why did the Agadir (Second Moroccan) Crisis of 1911 worsen international tension?
options: Germany sent a gunboat to challenge French influence in Morocco, drawing Britain closer to France
Italy withdrew from the Triple Alliance
questions.explain: Germany's dispatch of the gunboat Panther to Agadir alarmed Britain and strengthened the Anglo-French entente.

questions.q: A 1909 British cartoon shows Britain and Germany competing to launch ever-larger battleships. This competition is best described as the:
questions.explain: The rush to build dreadnought battleships after 1906 was the Anglo-German naval arms race, a key source of pre-war tension.

questions.q: According to Germany's Schlieffen Plan, which country was to be defeated quickly first before Germany turned to fight Russia?
questions.explain: The Schlieffen Plan aimed to knock out France rapidly in the west before Russia could fully mobilise in the east.
